'''''Antirrhinum tortuosum''''' is a species of plant in the family [[Plantaginaceae]].<ref name=POWO/><ref>{{Cite web|last=Mifsud|first=Stephen|date=2002-08-23|title=''Antirrhinum tortuosum'' (Greater Snapdragon) : MaltaWildPlants.com - the online Flora of the Maltese Islands.|url=https://www.maltawildplants.com/PLNT/Antirrhinum_tortuosum.php|access-date=2022-02-07|website=www.maltawildplants.com|language=en-us}}</ref> It is a herbaceous,<ref name=":0">{{Cite journal |last=Alaimo |first=Maria Grazia |last2=Melati |first2=Maria Rita |last3=Scialabba |first3=Anna |date=January 1997 |title=Pollen grain stereostructure, viability and germination; correlation with temperature of ''Antirrhinum tortuosum'' Bosc |url=http://www.tandfonline.com/doi/abs/10.1080/12538078.1997.10515763 |journal=Acta Botanica Gallica |language=en |volume=144 |issue=1 |pages=171–181 |doi=10.1080/12538078.1997.10515763 |issn=1253-8078}}</ref> perennial plant<ref name=":1">{{Cite journal |last=Mateu-Andres |first=I. |last2=De Paco |first2=L. |date=2006-08-22 |title=Genetic Diversity and the Reproductive System in Related Species of ''Antirrhinum'' |url=https://academic.oup.com/aob/article-lookup/doi/10.1093/aob/mcl186 |journal=Annals of Botany |language=en |volume=98 |issue=5 |pages=1053–1060 |doi=10.1093/aob/mcl186 |issn=0305-7364 |pmc=2803598 |pmid=17008348}}</ref> found naturally in the Western Mediterranean.<ref name=":2">{{Cite journal |last=Mateu-Andres |first=I. |date=2004-12-13 |title=Allozymic Differentiation of the ''Antirrhinum majus'' and ''A. siculum'' Species Groups |url=https://academic.oup.com/aob/article-lookup/doi/10.1093/aob/mci055 |journal=Annals of Botany |language=en |volume=95 |issue=3 |pages=465–473 |doi=10.1093/aob/mci055 |issn=0305-7364 |pmc=4246802 |pmid=15596453}}</ref><ref name=":3">{{Cite journal |last=Weiss |first=Julia |last2=Mühlemann |first2=Joëlle K. |last3=Ruiz-Hernández |first3=Victoria |last4=Dudareva |first4=Natalia |last5=Egea-Cortines |first5=Marcos |date=2016-12-21 |title=Phenotypic Space and Variation of Floral Scent Profiles during Late Flower Development in ''Antirrhinum'' |url=https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/plant-science/articles/10.3389/fpls.2016.01903/full |journal=Frontiers in Plant Science |language=English |volume=7 |doi=10.3389/fpls.2016.01903  |doi-access=free|issn=1664-462X|pmc=5174079 }}</ref>

== Description ==
These plants herbaceous with purple flowers, 30–35 mm in diameter, and grow on a [[raceme]].<ref name=":0" /> The plant flowers from spring through fall.<ref name=":0" /> and is perennial.<ref name=":1" />

== Habitat ==
This plant is commonly found growing out of limestone rockfaces, walls, or on roadsides.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":2" /> Populations often exist over small ranges.<ref name=":2" />
[[File:Wikidragons.jpg|thumb|Growing out of a stone wall in [[Dingli]], Malta]]

== Location ==
''Antirrhinum tortuosum'' is more widespread than other members of ''Antirrhinum'', found throughout the Western Mediterranean,<ref name=":1" /> significantly in Italy<ref name=":0" /> as well as the [[Iberian Peninsula]].<ref name=":2" /><ref name=":3" />

== Reproduction ==
It is a predominantly bee pollinated species<ref name=":3" /> with flowers forming a dense raceme.<ref name=":0" /> It is a fruit bearing species, and displays temperature-sensitive pollen germination.<ref name=":0" /> This species is also self incompatible.<ref name=":1" />
